title: Kaf
hookLine: kaf is a palm of the hand

cards: Hold out one hand, palm up. It's the shape of asking and the shape of offering: a beggar's hand looks like this, and so does a host's, saying come in, sit down. Now close it into a fist.
Same hand, different message. Turn it palm down: covering, keeping, holding back. A hand can say a lot without a word.
Hebrew has a word for the open, hollow part, the palm that can hold water or hold out bread. Today's letter carries that word as its name.

teach.h: THE SOLE OF THE DOVE'S FOOT.
teach.b: Kaf is the word for the palm of the hand, and the Bible uses it in more than one place. Start with a bird.
After the flood, Noah sends out a dove, and it comes back, because, in the King James, "the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot."

teach.h: HER PALM, OPEN TO THE POOR.
teach.b: In Hebrew, that sole is kaf too: the flat, open underside of a foot. So kaf is the part of you that meets the world, the palm that touches, the sole that stands. Next, a woman.
The poem at the end of Proverbs, praising a woman of valor, says: "She stretcheth out her hand to the poor." The Hebrew is kappah, her palm. She doesn't just give; she opens the flat of her hand.
Some families sing that poem at the Friday night table. Then, a question at the gate.

Psalm twenty-four asks who may go up into the hill of the LORD, and answers: "He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart." Clean hands, kapayim, palms again: not only what the hand gives, but what it has held.
Together, kaf becomes a little map of a life: where you stand, what you offer, what you've touched. And there's a plain fact of the body: a palm can't hold on and give at the same time.
The fingers have to open first. Opening the hand is already half the gift.

how: Some families sing Eshet Chayil, the poem from the end of Proverbs that includes 'she stretcheth out her hand to the poor', at the Friday night Sabbath table; children learning the alef-bet may meet kaf as the palm of a hand.

games.q: you're the dove Noah sent out after the flood. you fly and fly, and find nowhere to set the sole of your foot. what do you do?
o: keep flying until you find land.
return to Noah in the ark.
games.why: "the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark." the sole there is kaf.

practice: Rest your hands in your lap and close them gently into loose fists, noticing what you might be holding on to today: a worry, a grudge, a plan gripped too tightly.
Then slowly turn them over and open them, palms up, fingers relaxed, and breathe into the open space without forcing anything out. If you pray, you can pray with your palms like this.

wordCard.voice: Kaf. The palm of the hand, the sole of the foot: the open, flat part that stands, touches and gives. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: palm of the hand, sole of the foot; also the name of the letter kaf (כ).

carryVoice: Your line: open palm. Where you stand, what you offer, what you've touched. Back tomorrow, same hill.
